questions.question: Following the shoulder, the elbow is the second most common joint dislocation in adults. Which pattern is by far the most frequent?
questions.detail: Posterior dislocations are the most common pattern of elbow dislocation in adults.

questions.question: The 'terrible triad' of the elbow, a pattern of severe instability, consists of a posterior elbow dislocation combined with fractures of which two structures?
questions.detail: The 'terrible triad' involves a posterior dislocation along with fractures of the coronoid process and the radial head, indicating significant joint instability.

questions.question: In the initial stages of a posterior elbow dislocation, soft tissue damage typically first involves which structure?
questions.detail: Damage in a posterior dislocation typically begins on the lateral side, first involving the lateral ulnar collateral ligament (LUCL).

questions.question: What is the most common elbow fracture in adults?
questions.detail: Radial head fractures are the most frequent fractures encountered in the adult elbow.

questions.question: On a lateral elbow radiograph, which 'fat pad sign' is considered nearly diagnostic of a fracture in an adult patient?
choices: Visualization of the anterior fat pad (sail sign)
Elevation of the posterior fat pad
Obliteration of the supinator fat stripe
Absence of the anterior fat pad
questions.detail: Elevation of the posterior fat pad signifies a joint effusion and is nearly diagnostic of a fracture, typically of the radial head in adults.

questions.question: A 'Monteggia fracture-dislocation' is defined as:
choices: Fracture of the distal third of the radius with distal ulnar dislocation.
Fracture of the ulnar diaphysis with radial head dislocation at the elbow.
Radial head fracture with tearing of the interosseous membrane and DRUJ dislocation.
Intra-articular fracture of the distal radius with dorsal subluxation.
Avulsion of the medial epicondyle with elbow dislocation.
questions.detail: A Monteggia injury involves a fracture of the proximal-to-mid ulnar diaphysis and a dislocation of the radial head at the elbow.

questions.question: Which named injury involves a fracture of the distal third of the radius combined with a dislocation of the distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ)?
questions.detail: A Galeazzi fracture-dislocation is characterized by a fracture of the distal radius and dislocation of the distal radioulnar joint.

questions.question: An 'Essex-Lopresti fracture-dislocation' is characterized by a radial head fracture and dislocation of the DRUJ due to tearing of which structure?
questions.detail: This complex injury includes a radial head fracture, dislocation of the DRUJ, and a tear of the interosseous membrane.

questions.question: In athletes, tearing of the medial (ulnar) collateral ligament (MCL) is typically caused by which mechanism of injury?
questions.detail: Failure of the MCL is primarily caused by valgus stress, such as the tensile force generated during the late cocking phase of throwing.

questions.question: On a MR arthrogram of the elbow, the 'T-sign' (contrast tracking deep to the ligament) is indicative of a partial tear of which structure?
questions.detail: The 'T-sign' on MR arthrography represents undersurface stripping of the MCL attachment at the ulnar sublime tubercle.

questions.question: Which structure, when intact, helps prevent significant proximal retraction of a torn distal biceps tendon?
questions.detail: The bicipital aponeurosis (lacertus fibrosus) helps prevent proximal retraction of a torn distal biceps; if the tendon is significantly retracted, the lacertus is likely torn as well.

questions.question: Triceps tendon tears are relatively rare and frequently involve which radiographic finding?
questions.detail: Distal triceps tears are often associated with a bony avulsion at the insertion site on the olecranon.

questions.question: The pediatric elbow ossification centers generally appear in a specific order remembered by the mnemonic CRITOE. What structure does the 'I' represent?
questions.detail: The 'I' in CRITOE stands for the Internal (medial) epicondyle.

questions.question: In a normal pediatric elbow, the 'anterior humeral line' drawn along the anterior humeral cortex should pass through which part of the capitellum?
choices: It should not intersect the capitellum
questions.detail: In a normal elbow, the anterior humeral line should pass through the middle third of the ossified capitellum.

questions.question: Which radiographic line is used to evaluate for elbow dislocation or nursemaid's elbow by ensuring it passes through the capitellum on all views?
questions.detail: The radiocapitellar line, drawn through the radial shaft, must intersect the capitellum on every radiographic view; failure to do so suggests subluxation or dislocation.
